observations: The capsule SHA-256 and byte count, canonical source SHA-256, and canonical core-range SHA-256 all matched the metadata.
The assigned range specifies a coherent happy path from framework detection through catalog selection, project configuration, test-strategy generation, and evidence production.

The principal negative-space risks are mutable-catalog authority, state transitions, desired-versus-effective readiness, execution containment, evidence lifecycle, compatibility, test oracles, and cross-output reconciliation.

candidate_findings.title: Catalog-to-policy authority handoff is undefined
candidate_findings.gap: The range assigns discovery, permissions, and validation to the central tool registry and policy engine while separately calling GuiToolCatalog the single source of truth for framework-to-tool data. It does not define the mandatory handoff between those authorities or the result when catalog data and effective policy disagree.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A catalog-backed option could be displayed or propagated even when the runtime registry considers it unavailable or policy-denied, producing inconsistent GUI truth and potentially bypassing execution controls.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Field-level ownership, the mandatory policy-evaluation point, conflict precedence, synchronization semantics, and fail-closed behavior are underspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: - tool discovery, permissions, and validation live in the **central tool registry + policy engine** (not per-provider special cases)
Introduce a **single source of truth** for "GUI framework → available tools" so the interviewer (and any future automation) does not hardcode or duplicate this data.

candidate_findings.title: Mutable overlay ingestion has no trust or recovery contract
candidate_findings.gap: User-imported JSON and research-generated records can enter an overlay that wins by stable ID. The word "validated" is present, but the assigned range defines no validation criteria, provenance, authorization, collision handling, or corrupt-import recovery.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An untrusted, stale, or malformed entry can replace curated metadata and influence installation, selection, documentation lookup, or later execution.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Schema and integrity checks, provenance and trust levels, approval authority, permitted field semantics, collision and tombstone behavior, atomic import, quarantine, rollback, and audit history are underspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: editable via UI; export/import as JSON.
- Merge precedence: **overlay wins** by stable IDs (`framework_id`, `tool_id`).

- **Catalog population:** When the base+overlay `GuiToolCatalog` has no or sparse data for a framework, research can **add or extend overlay entries** (validated) so the catalog remains the single source of truth and future runs see the data. The user is shown **catalog-backed options** (including newly added entries), not a separate research-only result.

candidate_findings.title: Persisted tool choices are not bound to a catalog revision
candidate_findings.gap: The overlay can replace stable IDs and research can mutate it, while generated strategy content records selected tool IDs. No catalog revision, resolved-entry snapshot, or invalidation rule is specified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The same stored tool ID can resolve to different setup instructions or capabilities between interview, plan generation, and execution, making runs non-reproducible and silently changing user-approved behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Revision or hash binding, resolved tool and version snapshots, behavior for modified or deleted IDs, migration rules, and stale-selection invalidation are underspecified.

- **Framework tools:** List of selected framework tool IDs and how they are used (e.g. "Run Dioxus devtools for live preview; use for manual smoke checks" or "Run Iced headless runner with action set X").

candidate_findings.title: Multi-framework custom-headless state is under-cardinalized
candidate_findings.gap: Detection can yield multiple framework IDs and custom-headless defaults are described per framework, but the persisted custom-headless choice is a single Boolean with a single project-config projection.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A mixed GUI project cannot unambiguously express which framework needs custom automation, whether multiple runners coexist, or which runner Doctor and generated plans should evaluate.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Per-framework target association, multiple-runner coexistence and conflict semantics, per-target evidence identity, and revalidation when detected frameworks change are underspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Selection intent, installation, and effective readiness can be conflated
candidate_findings.gap: A plan/build preference writes a Doctor-readable project projection, while success is defined as Doctor verifying that a tool exists and runs. No state model distinguishes catalog-known, selected, planned, building, installed, callable, policy-denied, degraded, or stale.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The GUI, generated strategy, or runtime can present and use a merely planned tool as though it were operational; conversely, an existence check may pass without proving the selected capabilities or compatible version.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Requested-versus-effective readiness states, failure reasons, capability and version verification, check freshness, and the readiness gate controlling GUI and runtime claims are underspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: **Success criteria (how we know the plan succeeded):** (1) When a non-web GUI framework is detected, the interview offers framework tools and the custom headless option from the catalog. candidate_findings.title: Full evidence is retained without a privacy and capacity lifecycle
candidate_findings.gap: The custom runner emits timelines, summaries, screenshots or state dumps, manifests, and artifacts, while the evidence directory is allowlisted and never removed by prepare or cleanup. No local redaction, classification, retention, access, quota, or partial-run disposal contract appears in the assigned range.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: GUI artifacts and debug logs can persist credentials, personal data, proprietary content, and large binary output indefinitely, creating privacy exposure and unbounded disk growth.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Secret and sensitive-data handling, artifact access scope, retention and expiry, manual-prune ownership, quotas and backpressure, and cleanup semantics for failed or cancelled runs are underspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Agent-extensible action execution is not bound to a containment policy
candidate_findings.gap: The headless tool has an action catalog that agents can extend and execute, but the assigned range does not connect those actions to the central policy engine or define filesystem, network, credential, process, UI, or resource boundaries.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An automation action can mutate the project or host, access credentials, contact external systems, or continue after cancellation without an explicit authorization and containment model.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Actor authority, action capability declarations, policy evaluation, workspace boundaries, network and credential scopes, process and resource limits, timeout and cancellation behavior, and fail-closed cleanup are underspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Catalog entries lack compatibility and lifecycle dimensions

candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: A compatibility tuple, lifecycle and deprecation state, replacement semantics, support tier, version resolution, license constraints, verification requirements, and behavior for unsupported combinations are underspecified.
